chunks: Ibn Mahbūb narrated from Al-Ḥārith ibn Muḥammad, from Burayd Al-ʿIjlī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who came to his wife on a day that he was making up from the month of Ramadan, he عليه السلام said: “If he came to his wife before midday, then there is nothing upon him except one day in place of one day. And if he came to his wife after the sun’s zenith, then he must give charity to ten needy persons, for each needy person one mudd. If he is unable to do so, he fasts one day in place of one day and fasts three days as kaffarah for what he did.”

And it has been narrated: “If he broke his fast before midday, then there is nothing upon him; and if he broke his fast after midday, then kaffarah is upon him similar to what is upon one who broke a day from the month of Ramadan.”

key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, whose missed fast is being made up
key_terms.كَفَّارَةً: expiation required for invalidating the fast in the specified manner
key_terms.مَسَاكِينِ: needy persons who are to be fed as part of kaffarah
key_terms.مُدٌّ: a measured quantity of food given to each needy person
key_terms.يَقْضِيهِ: making up a missed obligatory fast
key_terms.يَوْمًا مَكَانَ يَوْمٍ: one replacement fast in place of the invalidated day
key_terms.ٱلزَّوَالِ: midday, the sun’s passing the zenith, which affects the legal ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the kaffarah for breaking a qada' fast of Ramadan after midday?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who invalidates a make-up fast of Ramadan by intercourse or breaking the fast. Before midday, the ruling is to make up the day again; after midday, an added kaffarah applies, either feeding ten needy persons or, if unable, fasting three additional days alongside the replacement fast. The report emphasizes the stricter ruling attached to violating a qada' fast after zawal.
